title: Bakery and Kitchen Again
premise: Theo Blackwood built a wedding-planning empire on the ruins of their own abandoned engagement, treating love as logistics and the heart as a muscle to be trained into obedience. When a letter Theo wrote eleven years ago — and never sent — surfaces in the estate of the late baker Marguerite Hale, it pulls Theo back to the small coastal town and to Juniper Hale, Marguerite's daughter, who once was everything and now wants answers. As Theo plans one final society wedding at the restored Hale bakery, the letter's truth forces a reckoning: Theo left not from lack of love but from terror of needing anyone. In the end, with the bakery's future and Juniper's forgiveness both hanging by a thread, Theo chooses the person over the career, sending the letter at last — by hand, in person — and staying.
about_author: Coral Winterbourne is the pen name of a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, where flour dusts everything like snow. She lives in a coastal town much like the one in her books, and insists that all her characters deserve bread and second chances.

chapters.title: The Unsent Postmark
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. While cataloguing the estate of deceased baker Marguerite Hale for a memorial wedding commission, Theo discovers an eleven-year-old unsent letter in their own handwriting, addressed to Juniper. Panic and denial: Theo burns nothing but pockets the letter instead. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism; the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper returns home to settle her mother's estate and finds the beloved bakery mortgaged to the brink, with a developer circling. She learns a famous wedding planner has taken the memorial commission — and recognizes the name before she recognizes the face. Emotional beat: grief braided with old anger; she came for closure, not reunion.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo and Juniper negotiate an uneasy alliance: Theo will plan the memorial event that could save the bakery if Juniper grants access to Marguerite's recipe archive. Neither mentions the letter. Theo rehearses containment — schedules, checklists, distance. Emotional beat: wary truce charged with everything unsaid.

chapters.title: What the Recipe Card Knew
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Sorting her mother's cards, Juniper finds annotations in Theo's handwriting from years ago — Marguerite had been mentoring them all along, secretly. The realization cracks Juniper's version of history: Theo didn't just vanish; someone stayed in touch. Emotional beat: betrayal complicated by tenderness.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wanted Everything
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's flagship client, a media heiress, demands the memorial date be moved to accommodate her own gala — threatening both the bakery timeline and Theo's firm. Theo's business partner pushes hard: drop the small-town job, protect the empire. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit; Theo feels the old machinery closing in.

chapters.title: Midnight Proofing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Unable to sleep, Juniper tests her mother's signature sourdough and finds Theo already in the kitchen at 3 a.m., unable to stay away either. Over rising dough they talk around the letter, and almost touch the truth. Emotional beat: warmth rekindling against both their wills; the heart refusing to be contained.

chapters.title: Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, flashback chapter. The night of the broken engagement: Theo's father's bankruptcy, the ultimatum, the letter written and hidden in Marguerite's care, and the train out of town. We finally see why Theo fled — not coldness, but the conviction that loving Juniper would destroy them both. Emotional beat: devastating context that reframes every scene before it.

chapters.title: The Letter, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper confronts Theo with the recipe-card evidence; cornered, Theo finally hands over the letter. Juniper reads it aloud in the empty bakery — a raw confession of fear, not absence of love. Then she asks the question Theo can't answer: why come back now? Emotional beat: catharsis that opens wounds rather than closing them.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The heiress's gala is moved onto the memorial date; the developer makes a cash offer Juniper can't refuse without the event proceeds; Theo's partner threatens to expose the letter as a publicity scandal. Forced to choose, Theo resigns mid-crisis, torching the career that saved everything. Emotional beat: climax — the muscle finally trained toward courage instead of control.

chapters.title: Bakery and Kitchen Again
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The memorial happens, smaller and imperfect, funded by the community Theo rallied after walking away from the firm. Weeks later, Theo returns not as a planner but as a person, delivering the letter by hand a second time — this time staying to watch it be read. The bakery reopens with both names on the door. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance reclaimed, identity chosen, survival redefined as belonging.
